correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=2, the deterministic separation inequalities force each ordered coordinate into a length-a band. In the critical window 1/n<r<1/(n-1), the bands are disjoint and each successful sample has exactly one point in the first band, giving the probability upper bound na by uniform marginal mass. A success/failure mixture with shifted arithmetic progression, randomized labels, and diagonal uniform complement gives exactly uniform one-dimensional marginals and event mass na. At equality the success event exhausts the marginal mass in every band; conditional ordered positions are uniform in their bands. Their translated offsets have equal means and are ordered, forcing identical offsets almost surely, hence the complete rigidity. Conditional label slot probabilities and uniform complement marginals follow from density balance. At the upper boundary, endpoint atomlessness kills the only geometrically possible configuration; at the lower boundary, rigid 1/n-spacing attains probability one. Larger critical threshold success is impossible for an optimizer at a smaller threshold. The standalone exact-rational checker runs 3128 finite identity assertions successfully; the analytic proof alone covers all real thresholds. No unproved nonstandard lemma or numerical extrapolation is required.

value.rationale: It solves a natural all-pairs hard-core exclusion event under arbitrary dependence uncertainty with an exact sharp envelope for every n and threshold. Its nontrivial contribution goes beyond a textbook union bound: saturation rigidifies all successful configurations into a uniformly shifted equispaced pattern and forces optimal tail probabilities at different critical thresholds to be mutually incompatible. This separates pointwise capacity from stochastic dominance for robust multi-point spacing and negative-dependence design, with a concrete intrinsic mathematical gap motivated by unrestricted-copula extremal statistics and max–min random spacings.
